summary.text: Mitosis is the part of the eukaryotic cell cycle in which replicated chromosomes are separated into two new nuclei.
It is an equational division that gives genetically identical cells in which the total number of chromosomes is maintained.
Chromosomes already duplicated in interphase condense and attach to spindle fibers that pull one copy of each to opposite sides of the cell.

facts.label: Stages
facts.value: Prophase through telophase, with preprophase in plant cells

facts.label: First description
facts.value: Wacław Mayzel described it in animal cells in 1875

facts.label: Human cells
facts.value: Most human cells are produced by mitosis

facts.label: Prokaryote alternative
facts.value: Bacteria and archaea divide by binary fission instead

items.prompt: After mitosis, a scientist compares a daughter cell with its parent. What does she find?

options.label: Half as many chromosomes, and a different mix of genes
The same number of chromosomes, and genetically identical
Twice as many chromosomes, with an identical mix of genes
The same number of chromosomes, but a new mix of genes

items.explain: Mitosis gives genetically identical cells in which the total number of chromosomes is maintained.

items.prompt: Why must a cell copy each chromosome before mitosis starts?

options.label: So the cell can pass half of its DNA to each of four daughters
So the nuclear envelope has something to break down around
So the spindle fibers have something to attach to in the cytoplasm
So each daughter cell can end up genetically identical to the parent

items.explain: Because each daughter cell should be genetically identical to the parent, the parent must make a copy of each chromosome before mitosis.

items.prompt: Under a microscope, a dividing cell's chromosomes separate inside an intact nucleus. Which kind of organism is most likely?

options.label: A fungus, since fungal cells generally have closed mitosis
An animal, since animal cells generally keep their nuclear envelope
A bacterium, since bacteria divide by mitosis inside the nucleus
A human egg, since egg cells are made by mitosis

items.explain: Fungal cells generally undergo closed mitosis, with chromosomes dividing inside an intact nucleus, while animal cells break down the nuclear envelope first.

items.prompt: Normal mitosis gives two daughter cells. If an error gives three or more, what can that cause?

options.label: Cells with half the usual number of chromosomes
Faster, healthier division that repairs damage
Non-viable embryos that fail to implant
A switch to binary fission inside the same cell

items.explain: Errors that produce three or more daughter cells can be the cause of non-viable embryos that fail to implant.

items.prompt: Most human cells are produced by mitotic division. Which human cells are made a different way?

options.label: Nerve cells, which come from binary fission
Blood cells, which come from meiosis
Bone cells, which come from amitosis
Sperm and egg cells, which come from meiosis

items.explain: The gametes, sperm and egg cells, are important exceptions because they are produced by meiosis.

items.prompt: Mitosis separates chromosomes into two new nuclei. How do bacteria, which lack a true nucleus, divide?

options.label: By a smaller version of mitosis
By a different process called binary fission
By meiosis, since there is no nucleus
By budding off a nucleus first

items.explain: Prokaryotes, which lack a true nucleus, divide by a different process called binary fission.
